Abu Raja' and Hamzah read وَالسَّاعَةَ (al-sa'ata) in the accusative, coordinating it with "the promise." ﴿"There is no doubt in it"﴾ ... ﴿"You said: 'We do not know what the Hour is; we only think it is a conjecture, and we are not certain."﴾ That it will happen. ﴿And there will appear to them the evil of what they did,﴾ that is, its recompense. ﴿And there will surround them what they used to mock.﴾ And it is said: ﴿"Today We will forget you as you forgot the meeting of this your Day,"﴾ that is, We will leave you in the Fire. ﴿As you forgot the meeting of this your Day,﴾ as you abandoned faith in this your Day. ﴿Your refuge is the Fire, and you have no helpers.﴾ ﴿That is because you took the signs of Allah in mockery, and the life of this world deceived you.﴾ ﴿So today they will not be brought out from it,﴾ the common readers read يُخْرَجُونَ (yukhrajuna) with a damma on the ya', while the people of Kufa except 'Asim read it with a fatha on it.

﴿Nor will they be asked to make amends (yustatabun), that is, to be pleased.﴾ ﴿So to Allah belongs all praise, Lord of the heavens and Lord of the earth, Lord of the worlds.﴾ The common readers read رَبِّ (rabbi) with a kasra on the ba' in all three, while Ibn Muhaysin read it in the nominative, meaning "He is the Lord."

﴿And to Him belongs the greatness in the heavens and the earth, and He is the Mighty, the Wise.﴾

﴿And Allah created the heavens and the earth in truth, and so that every soul may be recompensed for what it has earned, and they will not be wronged. Have you seen him who takes his desire as his god?﴾

Ibn 'Abbas, al-Husayn and Qatadah said: That refers to the disbeliever who takes his religion to be whatever he desires. He does not desire anything without doing it. He does not believe in Allah, does not fear Him, does not forbid what Allah has forbidden, and does not permit what Allah has permitted. His religion is only what his soul desires, and he acts upon it, and piety does not restrain him from it.

Others said: The meaning is, "Have you seen him who takes his object of worship to be his desire, so that he worships whatever he desires?"

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: For some time the Quraysh worshipped al-'Uzza, which was a white stone, and the Arabs worshipped stones, gold and silver. Whenever they found something better than the first, they threw away or broke the first, or threw it into a well, and worshipped the other. So Allah the Exalted revealed this verse.

Muqatil said: It was revealed concerning al-Harith ibn Qays al-Tamimi, one of the reckless ones (al-mustahtirun), because he worshipped whatever his soul desired.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us: Talhah and 'Ubayd Allah narrated to us, both saying: Ibn Mujahid narrated to us, Ibn Abi Mihran narrated to me, Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Abi 'Umar narrated to us, who said: Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah said: They only worshipped stones because the House (the Ka'bah) is made of stones.

Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: In this verse there is an inversion (taqdim wa ta'khir), and its meaning is: "Have you seen him who takes his desire as his god?"

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us: 'Ubayd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Shanbah narrated to us, Muhammad ibn 'Imran ibn Harun narrated to us, Abu 'Ubayd Allah al-Makhzumi narrated to us, Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah narrated to us, from Ibn Shubrumah, from al-Sha'bi, who said: Desire (al-hawa) was only so named because it plunges its companion into the Fire (yahwi).

And with this chain, from Sufyan, from Sulayman al-Ahwal, from Tawus, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Allah the Mighty and Majestic did not mention desire (hawa) in the Qur'an except to condemn it.

Abu Umamah narrated from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "No god under the sky is more hateful to Allah than desire." [221] [Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 16/167.]

And the Prophet ﷺ said: "Three things destroy: stinginess that is obeyed, desire that is followed, and a man's self-admiration." [222] [al-Mu'jam al-Awsat: 5/328; Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 16/167.]

Damrah ibn Habib narrated from Shaddad ibn Aws that the Prophet ﷺ said: "The intelligent one is he who holds himself accountable and works for what comes after death, and the wicked one is he who follows his soul's desires and entertains wishful hopes about Allah." [223] [Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 16/167.]

Mudar the judge said: Carving mountains with fingernails until the joints are cut apart is easier than opposing desire once it has taken hold of souls.

Ibn al-Muqaffa' was asked about desire (al-hawa), and he said: "It is humiliation (hawan) whose nun has been stolen," and a poet versified it:

The nun of humiliation has been stolen from desire,
So when you desire, you have met with humiliation.

Another said:

Desire is in essence humiliation itself,
So when you desire, you have earned humiliation.

And when you desire, desire may have made you its slave,
So submit to your love, whoever it may be.

Abu al-Qasim al-Habibi recited to us; Abu Hatim Muhammad ibn Hayyan al-Masni recited to us, and said: "I have not seen anything more complete than it." He said: Muhammad ibn 'Ali al-Halari recited to us a verse by 'Abd Allah al-Mubarak:

Among the signs of affliction for the afflicted is
That you find no withdrawal from your desire.

The slave is the slave of the self in its appetites,
While the free man may be sated at times and hungry at others.

Abu al-Qasim al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Habibi recited to us; Abu al-Hasan 'Isa ibn Zayd al-'Uqayli recited to us; Abu al-Muthanna Mu'adh ibn al-Muthanna al-'Anbari recited to us, from his father, for Abu al-'Atahiyah:

Disobey the desire of the self and do not obey it,
For if you anger it, it will [still] be against you.

Until when will you seek its pleasure,
While it seeks your enmity?

Abu al-Qasim al-Habibi recited to us; Abu 'Ubayd al-Tusi recited to us:

If you give the self its wishes,
It will open its mouth wide toward its desire.

I heard Abu al-Qasim say: I heard Abu Nasr ibn Mansur ibn 'Abd Allah al-Isfahani say in Herat:

I heard Abu al-Hasan 'Amr ibn Wasil al-Bahtari say: Sahl ibn 'Abd Allah al-Tustari was asked about desire, and he said to the questioner: "Your desire commands you; if you oppose it, it will destroy you." And he said: "When two matters present themselves to you and you are uncertain which is better, look at the one farther from your desire, for it..."

Abu al-Qasim al-Habibi recited to us, the Imam Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Isma'il al-Qaffal al-Mashashi in Marw recited to us, and Abu Bakr al-Zaydi recited to me:

When the self demands from you a desire one day,
And there is a path to opposing it,

Leave it and oppose what you desire, for
Your desire is an enemy, and opposition is a friend.

Allah the Glorified and Exalted said:

﴿And Allah has led him astray knowing about him, and has sealed his hearing and his heart, and placed a covering upon his sight.﴾ Hamzah, al-Kisa'i and Khalaf read غَشْوَةً (ghashwatan), with a fatha on the ghayn and without an alif, while the rest read غِشاوَةً (ghishawatan), with an alif and a kasra on the ghayn.

﴿So who will guide him after Allah? Will you not then take heed?﴾ And they said, meaning the polytheists:

﴿There is nothing but our life of this world: we die and we live, and nothing destroys us except time.﴾ "We die and live": the fathers die and the sons live. "And nothing destroys us except time": nothing ends us except the age and the length of life. In the reading of Ibn Mas'ud it is: "And nothing destroys us except time passes."

﴿And they have no knowledge of that; they only conjecture.﴾

Then Allah the Exalted said in His Book: ﴿There is nothing but our life of this world: we die and we live, and nothing destroys us except time﴾, so they curse time.

Allah the Exalted said: "The son of Adam hurts Me: he curses time, while I am Time. In My hand is the command; I alternate the night and the day." [224] [Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 25/198.]

Abu Sa'id Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Hamdun informed us, with my reading to him in Safar of the year 388, and he acknowledged it: Abu Hamid Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan informed us; Muhammad ibn Yahya, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Bishr and Ahmad ibn Yusuf narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq ibn Hammam narrated to us, Ma'mar ibn Rashid informed us, from Hammam ibn Munabbih ibn Kamil ibn Sayj, who said: This is what Abu Hurayrah narrated to us from Muhammad ﷺ, who said: "Allah the Exalted said: Let not the son of Adam say, 'O misfortune of time,' for I am Time. I send the night and the day, and when I wish, I seize them." [225] [Fath al-Bari: 10/466; Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 14/1.]

Abu 'Abd Allah ibn Fanjawayh informed us: 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Samurah narrated to us; 'Abd al-Malik ibn Ahmad al-Baghdadi narrated to us; Mahmud ibn Khadash narrated to us; Sufyan ibn Muhammad al-Thawri narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: "Do not curse time, for Allah the Exalted is Time." [226] [Musnad Ahmad: 2/395.]

Abu 'Ubayd al-Qasim ibn Sallam said in explaining this hadith: This is something that no one among the people of Islam should be ignorant of its meaning. The Arabs' custom was to blame time at the time of calamities and misfortunes, when time destroyed them, the days frightened them, and the age came upon them, and similar things, until they mentioned it in their poetry, [and attributed events to it] (addition from Tafsir al-Qurtubi).

'Amr ibn Qami'ah said:

The daughters of time have shot at me from where I do not see,
So how about one who is shot at and is not a shooter?

If they were arrows, I would have guarded against them,
But I am being shot at with no arrows.

On both palms once, and on a staff,
I rise three times after my standing.

It is related that al-Sha'bi entered upon 'Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan when he had become weak, and [the caliph] asked him about his condition, so he recited these verses:

Time has taken them away this morning,
And time shoots at me and I do not shoot.

O time, you have greatly afflicted us
With our best, and it has settled in our bones.

You have left us as meat upon a chopping block;
If you were to spare any of the meat...

And you have taken from us what you will not return to us.
O time, you have not been just in judgment.

Abu al-Qasim al-Sadusi recited to us; 'Abd al-Sami' ibn Muhammad al-Hashimi recited to us; Abu al-Hasan al-'Absi informed us, about Ibn Lankak on this theme:

Say to time, emptied of nobility, O you ugly in deeds, stern of countenance,
How many a noble man you have brought down to the lowlands, and how many a base man you have raised to the Pleiades.

Abu 'Ubaydah said: I debated with some of the heretics (mulahidah). He said: "Do you not see that He says: 'Indeed Allah is Time'?" I said to him: "Did anyone ever revile Allah in the calamities of time? Rather, they used to say as al-A'sha said:

Allah has taken [the people] for fidelity and justice,
And has turned blame toward the man..."

He said: So the interpretation of the Prophet's saying ﷺ "Indeed Allah is Time" is that Allah, Majestic is His mention, is the One who brings time, hardships and calamities. So if you revile time, the reviling falls upon Allah the Exalted, because He is the doer of these things, its judge and its manager.

Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: Its meaning: "Indeed Allah is the one who makes time (mudahhir al-duhur)."

It is related from 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, in one of his sermons: "The one who makes times, from whom is ease, and from whom is hardship."

The proof of this interpretation is what al-Qasim al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Nisaburi informed us: Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Karizi narrated to us; Abu 'Abd Allah Muhammad ibn al-Qasim al-Jumahi narrated to us; 'Asr ibn Ahmad narrated to us, who said: It reached me that Salim ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar often mentioned time, so Abu 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar rebuked him and said: "O my son, beware of mentioning time," and he recited:

Time is not the one who commits a thing at its time,
Nor the bringer of trials, so do not revile time.

But whenever Allah sends a sender
Upon a people, He makes their ease into hardship.

Abu al-Qasim al-Habibi recited to us; the Shaykh Abu Muhammad Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Muzani recited to us; Mu'adh ibn Najdah ibn al-'Iryan recited to us:

Time turns over matters, for it [if it] has struck you with pains,
And the one who has time upon him for blame, for time only relates the course of pens.

Time is complained of, and is asked for more, but
The command of the King is the support of rulings.

Al-Ustadh Abu al-Qasim recited to us; my father recited to me; Abu 'Ali Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Wahhab al-Thaqafi recited to me:

O one who blames time when it befalls him,
Do not blame time for its excuse.

Time is commanded by one who commands it,
And time ends at his command.

How many a disbeliever has abundant wealth
That increases manifold in his disbelief.

And a believer who has not a dirham
Whose faith increases in his poverty.

﴿And when Our clear verses are recited to them, their argument is nothing but that they say: "Bring our fathers, if you are truthful." Say: "Allah gives you life, then causes you to die, then will gather you to the Day of Resurrection," about which there is no doubt, but most people do not know.﴾ (That is, to the Day of Resurrection.) ﴿And to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. And on the Day the Hour is established, on that Day the falsifiers will lose. And you will see every nation kneeling (jathiyah), gathered, sitting on its knees from the terror of that Day. The root of jathwah is a group of anything.﴾

Tarafah, describing two graves, said:

You see two heaps of earth upon them,
Slabs, hard, of smooth stone.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us: 'Umar ibn Nuh al-Bajali narrated to us; Abu Khalifah narrated to us; 'Uthman ibn 'Abd Allah al-Shami narrated to us; 'Uqbah ibn al-Walid narrated to us, from Artat ibn al-Mundhir, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The first thing Allah created was the pen, from light, the distance of whose travel is five hundred years; and the Tablet, from light, the distance of whose travel is five hundred years. Abu Sa'id Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Hamdun informed us, with my reading to him in Safar of the year 388, and he acknowledged it: Abu Hamid Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan informed us; Muhammad ibn Yahya, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Bishr and Ahmad ibn Yusuf narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq ibn Hammam narrated to us, Ma'mar ibn Rashid informed us, from Hammam ibn Munabbih ibn Kamil ibn Sayj, who said: This is what Abu Hurayrah narrated to us from Muhammad ﷺ, who said: "Allah the Exalted said: Let not the son of Adam say, 'O misfortune of time,' for I am Time. I send the night and the day, and when I wish, I seize them." [225] [Fath al-Bari: 10/466; Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 14/1.]

Abu 'Abd Allah ibn Fanjawayh informed us: 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Samurah narrated to us; 'Abd al-Malik ibn Ahmad al-Baghdadi narrated to us; Mahmud ibn Khadash narrated to us; Sufyan ibn Muhammad al-Thawri narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: "Do not curse time, for Allah the Exalted is Time." [226] [Musnad Ahmad: 2/395.]

Abu 'Ubayd al-Qasim ibn Sallam said in explaining this hadith: This is something that no one among the people of Islam should be ignorant of its meaning. The Arabs' custom was to blame time at the time of calamities and misfortunes, when time destroyed them, the days frightened them, and the age came upon them, and similar things, until they mentioned it in their poetry, [and attributed events to it] (addition from Tafsir al-Qurtubi).

'Amr ibn Qami'ah said:

The daughters of time have shot at me from where I do not see,
So how about one who is shot at and is not a shooter?

If they were arrows, I would have guarded against them,
But I am being shot at with no arrows.

On both palms once, and on a staff,
I rise three times after my standing.

It is related that al-Sha'bi entered upon 'Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan when he had become weak, and [the caliph] asked him about his condition, so he recited these verses:

Time has taken them away this morning,
And time shoots at me and I do not shoot.

O time, you have greatly afflicted us
With our best, and it has settled in our bones.

You have left us as meat upon a chopping block;
If you were to spare any of the meat...

And you have taken from us what you will not return to us.
O time, you have not been just in judgment.

Abu al-Qasim al-Sadusi recited to us; 'Abd al-Sami' ibn Muhammad al-Hashimi recited to us; Abu al-Hasan al-'Absi informed us, about Ibn Lankak on this theme:

Say to time, emptied of nobility, O you ugly in deeds, stern of countenance,
How many a noble man you have brought down to the lowlands, and how many a base man you have raised to the Pleiades.

Abu 'Ubaydah said: I debated with some of the heretics (mulahidah). He said: "Do you not see that He says: 'Indeed Allah is Time'?" I said to him: "Did anyone ever revile Allah in the calamities of time? Rather, they used to say as al-A'sha said:

Allah has taken [the people] for fidelity and justice,
And has turned blame toward the man..."

He said: So the interpretation of the Prophet's saying ﷺ "Indeed Allah is Time" is that Allah, Majestic is His mention, is the One who brings time, hardships and calamities. So if you revile time, the reviling falls upon Allah the Exalted, because He is the doer of these things, its judge and its manager.

Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: Its meaning: "Indeed Allah is the one who makes time (mudahhir al-duhur)."

It is related from 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, in one of his sermons: "The one who makes times, from whom is ease, and from whom is hardship."

The proof of this interpretation is what al-Qasim al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Nisaburi informed us: Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Karizi narrated to us; Abu 'Abd Allah Muhammad ibn al-Qasim al-Jumahi narrated to us; 'Asr ibn Ahmad narrated to us, who said: It reached me that Salim ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar often mentioned time, so Abu 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar rebuked him and said: "O my son, beware of mentioning time," and he recited:

Time is not the one who commits a thing at its time,
Nor the bringer of trials, so do not revile time.

But whenever Allah sends a sender
Upon a people, He makes their ease into hardship.

Abu al-Qasim al-Habibi recited to us; the Shaykh Abu Muhammad Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Muzani recited to us; Mu'adh ibn Najdah ibn al-'Iryan recited to us:

Time turns over matters, for it [if it] has struck you with pains,
And the one who has time upon him for blame, for time only relates the course of pens.

Time is complained of, and is asked for more, but
The command of the King is the support of rulings.

Al-Ustadh Abu al-Qasim recited to us; my father recited to me; Abu 'Ali Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Wahhab al-Thaqafi recited to me:

O one who blames time when it befalls him,
Do not blame time for its excuse.

Time is commanded by one who commands it,
And time ends at his command.

How many a disbeliever has abundant wealth
That increases manifold in his disbelief.

And a believer who has not a dirham
Whose faith increases in his poverty.

﴿And when Our clear verses are recited to them, their argument is nothing but that they say: "Bring our fathers, if you are truthful." Say: "Allah gives you life, then causes you to die, then will gather you to the Day of Resurrection," about which there is no doubt, but most people do not know.﴾ (That is, to the Day of Resurrection.) ﴿And to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. And on the Day the Hour is established, on that Day the falsifiers will lose. And you will see every nation kneeling (jathiyah), gathered, sitting on its knees from the terror of that Day. The root of jathwah is a group of anything.﴾

Tarafah, describing two graves, said:

You see two heaps of earth upon them,
Slabs, hard, of smooth stone.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us: 'Abd Allah ibn Yusuf narrated to us; Musa ibn Muhammad al-Halwani narrated to us; Ya'qub ibn Ishaq al-'Alawi narrated to us; 'Abd Allah ibn Yahya al-Thaqafi narrated to us; Abu 'Ilran narrated to us, from 'Asim al-Ahwal, from Ibn 'Uthman al-Nahdi, from Salman al-Farisi, who said: On the Day of Resurrection there is an hour that lasts ten years, in which people will be kneeling on their knees, until even Ibrahim (peace be upon him) will call out: "I ask nothing of You today except for myself."

﴿Every nation will be called to its record. Today you will be recompensed for what you used to do. This is Our Book, which speaks against you with truth.﴾ In it is the register of the guardians (diwan al-hafazah); and it was said: it is the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz).

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us: 'Umar ibn Nuh al-Bajali narrated to us; Abu Khalifah narrated to us; 'Uthman ibn 'Abd Allah al-Shami narrated to us; 'Uqbah ibn al-Walid narrated to us, from Artat ibn al-Mundhir, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The first thing Allah created was the pen, from light, the distance of whose travel is five hundred years; and the Tablet, from light, the distance of whose travel is five hundred years. He said to the pen: 'Write,' and it wrote what would be until the Day of Resurrection, its coolness and its heat, its moist and its dry." Then he recited this verse: ﴿This is Our Book, which speaks against you with truth.﴾ [228] [al-Mustadrak: 2/498; Fath al-Bari: 6/206; Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 29/22; Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 3/245.]

﴿Indeed We were having your deeds copied.﴾ He said: Can copying (naskh) occur except from a book that has been completed? The meaning of nastansikh is: He commands copying. Al-Dahhak said: "We recorded (nuthbit)." Al-Suddi: "We wrote." Al-Hasan: "We preserved."

﴿As for those who believed and did righteous deeds, their Lord will admit them into His mercy, that is, His Paradise. That is the clear triumph, the pure victory. And as for those who disbelieved: "Were not My verses recited to you? But you were arrogant and were a criminal people."﴾ And when it is said, ﴿"Indeed the promise of Allah is true, and the Hour, there is no doubt about it,"﴾ the common readers read وَالسَّاعَةُ (al-sa'atu) in the nominative, as a beginning (mubtada') with its predicate in what follows; their evidence is His saying: ﴿Indeed the earth belongs to Allah; He gives it as inheritance to whom He wills of His servants, and the final outcome is for the God-fearing.﴾ [Surah al-A'raf: 128.]

Abu Raja' and Hamzah read وَالسَّاعَةَ (al-sa'ata) in the accusative, coordinating it with "the promise." ﴿"There is no doubt in it"﴾ ... ﴿"You said: 'We do not know what the Hour is; we only think it is a conjecture, and we are not certain."﴾ That it will happen. ﴿And there will appear to them the evil of what they did,﴾ that is, its recompense. ﴿And there will surround them what they used to mock.﴾ And it is said: ﴿"Today We will forget you as you forgot the meeting of this your Day,"﴾ that is, We will leave you in the Fire. ﴿As you forgot the meeting of this your Day,﴾ as you abandoned faith in this your Day. ﴿Your refuge is the Fire, and you have no helpers.﴾ ﴿That is because you took the signs of Allah in mockery, and the life of this world deceived you.﴾ ﴿So today they will not be brought out from it,﴾ the common readers read يُخْرَجُونَ (yukhrajuna) with a damma on the ya', while the people of Kufa except 'Asim read it with a fatha on it.

﴿Nor will they be asked to make amends (yustatabun), that is, to be pleased.﴾ ﴿So to Allah belongs all praise, Lord of the heavens and Lord of the earth, Lord of the worlds.﴾ The common readers read رَبِّ (rabbi) with a kasra on the ba' in all three, while Ibn Muhaysin read it in the nominative, meaning "He is the Lord."

﴿And to Him belongs the greatness in the heavens and the earth, and He is the Mighty, the Wise.﴾

﴿And Allah created the heavens and the earth in truth, and so that every soul may be recompensed for what it has earned, and they will not be wronged. Have you seen him who takes his desire as his god?﴾

Ibn 'Abbas, al-Husayn and Qatadah said: That refers to the disbeliever who takes his religion to be whatever he desires. He does not desire anything without doing it. He does not believe in Allah, does not fear Him, does not forbid what Allah has forbidden, and does not permit what Allah has permitted. His religion is only what his soul desires, and he acts upon it, and piety does not restrain him from it.

Others said: The meaning is, "Have you seen him who takes his object of worship to be his desire, so that he worships whatever he desires?"

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: For some time the Quraysh worshipped al-'Uzza, which was a white stone, and the Arabs worshipped stones, gold and silver. Whenever they found something better than the first, they threw away or broke the first, or threw it into a well, and worshipped the other. So Allah the Exalted revealed this verse.

Muqatil said: It was revealed concerning al-Harith ibn Qays al-Tamimi, one of the reckless ones (al-mustahtirun), because he worshipped whatever his soul desired.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us: Talhah and 'Ubayd Allah narrated to us, both saying: Ibn Mujahid narrated to us, Ibn Abi Mihran narrated to me, Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Abi 'Umar narrated to us, who said: Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah said: They only worshipped stones because the House (the Ka'bah) is made of stones.

Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: In this verse there is an inversion (taqdim wa ta'khir), and its meaning is: "Have you seen him who takes his desire as his god?"

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us: 'Ubayd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Shanbah narrated to us, Muhammad ibn 'Imran ibn Harun narrated to us, Abu 'Ubayd Allah al-Makhzumi narrated to us, Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah narrated to us, from Ibn Shubrumah, from al-Sha'bi, who said: Desire (al-hawa) was only so named because it plunges its companion into the Fire (yahwi).

And with this chain, from Sufyan, from Sulayman al-Ahwal, from Tawus, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Allah the Mighty and Majestic did not mention desire (hawa) in the Qur'an except to condemn it.

Abu Umamah narrated from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "No god under the sky is more hateful to Allah than desire." [221] [Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 16/167.]

And the Prophet ﷺ said: "Three things destroy: stinginess that is obeyed, desire that is followed, and a man's self-admiration." [222] [al-Mu'jam al-Awsat: 5/328; Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 16/167.]

Damrah ibn Habib narrated from Shaddad ibn Aws that the Prophet ﷺ said: "The intelligent one is he who holds himself accountable and works for what comes after death, and the wicked one is he who follows his soul's desires and entertains wishful hopes about Allah." [223] [Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 16/167.]

Mudar the judge said: Carving mountains with fingernails until the joints are cut apart is easier than opposing desire once it has taken hold of souls.

Ibn al-Muqaffa' was asked about desire (al-hawa), and he said: "It is humiliation (hawan) whose nun has been stolen," and a poet versified it:

The nun of humiliation has been stolen from desire,
So when you desire, you have met with humiliation.

Another said:

Desire is in essence humiliation itself,
So when you desire, you have earned humiliation.

And when you desire, desire may have made you its slave,
So submit to your love, whoever it may be.

Abu al-Qasim al-Habibi recited to us; Abu Hatim Muhammad ibn Hayyan al-Masni recited to us, and said: "I have not seen anything more complete than it." He said: Muhammad ibn 'Ali al-Halari recited to us a verse by 'Abd Allah al-Mubarak:

Among the signs of affliction for the afflicted is
That you find no withdrawal from your desire.

The slave is the slave of the self in its appetites,
While the free man may be sated at times and hungry at others.

Abu al-Qasim al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Habibi recited to us; Abu al-Hasan 'Isa ibn Zayd al-'Uqayli recited to us; Abu al-Muthanna Mu'adh ibn al-Muthanna al-'Anbari recited to us, from his father, for Abu al-'Atahiyah:

Disobey the desire of the self and do not obey it,
For if you anger it, it will [still] be against you.

Until when will you seek its pleasure,
While it seeks your enmity?

Abu al-Qasim al-Habibi recited to us; Abu 'Ubayd al-Tusi recited to us:

If you give the self its wishes,
It will open its mouth wide toward its desire.

I heard Abu al-Qasim say: I heard Abu Nasr ibn Mansur ibn 'Abd Allah al-Isfahani say in Herat:

I heard Abu al-Hasan 'Amr ibn Wasil al-Bahtari say: Sahl ibn 'Abd Allah al-Tustari was asked about desire, and he said to the questioner: "Your desire commands you; if you oppose it, it will destroy you." And he said: "When two matters present themselves to you and you are uncertain which is better, look at the one farther from your desire, for it..."

When the self demands from you a desire one day,
And there is a path to opposing it,

Leave it and oppose what you desire, for
Your desire is an enemy, and opposition is a friend.

Allah the Glorified and Exalted said:

﴿And Allah has led him astray knowing about him, and has sealed his hearing and his heart, and placed a covering upon his sight.﴾ Hamzah, al-Kisa'i and Khalaf read غَشْوَةً (ghashwatan), with a fatha on the ghayn and without an alif, while the rest read غِشاوَةً (ghishawatan), with an alif and a kasra on the ghayn.

﴿So who will guide him after Allah? Will you not then take heed?﴾ And they said, meaning the polytheists:

﴿There is nothing but our life of this world: we die and we live, and nothing destroys us except time.﴾ "We die and live": the fathers die and the sons live. "And nothing destroys us except time": nothing ends us except the age and the length of life. In the reading of Ibn Mas'ud it is: "And nothing destroys us except time passes."

﴿And they have no knowledge of that; they only conjecture.﴾

And as for those who disbelieved: "Were not My verses recited to you? But you were arrogant and were a criminal people."﴾ And when it is said, ﴿"Indeed the promise of Allah is true, and the Hour, there is no doubt about it,"﴾ the common readers read وَالسَّاعَةُ (al-sa'atu) in the nominative, as a beginning (mubtada') with its predicate in what follows; their evidence is His saying: ﴿Indeed the earth belongs to Allah; He gives it as inheritance to whom He wills of His servants, and the final outcome is for the God-fearing.﴾ [Surah al-A'raf: 128.]

Abu Raja' and Hamzah read وَالسَّاعَةَ (al-sa'ata) in the accusative, coordinating it with "the promise." ﴿"There is no doubt in it"﴾ ... ﴿"You said: 'We do not know what the Hour is; we only think it is a conjecture, and we are not certain."﴾ That it will happen. ﴿And there will appear to them the evil of what they did,﴾ that is, its recompense. ﴿And there will surround them what they used to mock.﴾ And it is said: ﴿"Today We will forget you as you forgot the meeting of this your Day,"﴾ that is, We will leave you in the Fire. ﴿As you forgot the meeting of this your Day,﴾ as you abandoned faith in this your Day. ﴿Your refuge is the Fire, and you have no helpers.﴾ ﴿That is because you took the signs of Allah in mockery, and the life of this world deceived you.﴾ ﴿So today they will not be brought out from it,﴾ the common readers read يُخْرَجُونَ (yukhrajuna) with a damma on the ya', while the people of Kufa except 'Asim read it with a fatha on it.

﴿Nor will they be asked to make amends (yustatabun), that is, to be pleased.﴾ ﴿So to Allah belongs all praise, Lord of the heavens and Lord of the earth, Lord of the worlds.﴾ The common readers read رَبِّ (rabbi) with a kasra on the ba' in all three, while Ibn Muhaysin read it in the nominative, meaning "He is the Lord."

﴿And to Him belongs the greatness in the heavens and the earth, and He is the Mighty, the Wise.﴾

﴿And Allah created the heavens and the earth in truth, and so that every soul may be recompensed for what it has earned, and they will not be wronged. Have you seen him who takes his desire as his god?﴾

Ibn 'Abbas, al-Husayn and Qatadah said: That refers to the disbeliever who takes his religion to be whatever he desires. He does not desire anything without doing it. He does not believe in Allah, does not fear Him, does not forbid what Allah has forbidden, and does not permit what Allah has permitted. His religion is only what his soul desires, and he acts upon it, and piety does not restrain him from it.

Others said: The meaning is, "Have you seen him who takes his object of worship to be his desire, so that he worships whatever he desires?"

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: For some time the Quraysh worshipped al-'Uzza, which was a white stone, and the Arabs worshipped stones, gold and silver. Whenever they found something better than the first, they threw away or broke the first, or threw it into a well, and worshipped the other. So Allah the Exalted revealed this verse.

Muqatil said: It was revealed concerning al-Harith ibn Qays al-Tamimi, one of the reckless ones (al-mustahtirun), because he worshipped whatever his soul desired.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us: Talhah and 'Ubayd Allah narrated to us, both saying: Ibn Mujahid narrated to us, Ibn Abi Mihran narrated to me, Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Abi 'Umar narrated to us, who said: Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah said: They only worshipped stones because the House (the Ka'bah) is made of stones.

Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: In this verse there is an inversion (taqdim wa ta'khir), and its meaning is: "Have you seen him who takes his desire as his god?"

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us: 'Ubayd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Shanbah narrated to us, Muhammad ibn 'Imran ibn Harun narrated to us, Abu 'Ubayd Allah al-Makhzumi narrated to us, Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah narrated to us, from Ibn Shubrumah, from al-Sha'bi, who said: Desire (al-hawa) was only so named because it plunges its companion into the Fire (yahwi).

And with this chain, from Sufyan, from Sulayman al-Ahwal, from Tawus, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Allah the Mighty and Majestic did not mention desire (hawa) in the Qur'an except to condemn it.

Abu Umamah narrated from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "No god under the sky is more hateful to Allah than desire." [221] [Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 16/167.]

And the Prophet ﷺ said: "Three things destroy: stinginess that is obeyed, desire that is followed, and a man's self-admiration." [222] [al-Mu'jam al-Awsat: 5/328; Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 16/167.]

Damrah ibn Habib narrated from Shaddad ibn Aws that the Prophet ﷺ said: "The intelligent one is he who holds himself accountable and works for what comes after death, and the wicked one is he who follows his soul's desires and entertains wishful hopes about Allah." [223] [Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 16/167.]

Mudar the judge said: Carving mountains with fingernails until the joints are cut apart is easier than opposing desire once it has taken hold of souls.

Ibn al-Muqaffa' was asked about desire (al-hawa), and he said: "It is humiliation (hawan) whose nun has been stolen," and a poet versified it:

The nun of humiliation has been stolen from desire,
So when you desire, you have met with humiliation.

Another said:

Desire is in essence humiliation itself,
So when you desire, you have earned humiliation.

And when you desire, desire may have made you its slave,
So submit to your love, whoever it may be.

Abu al-Qasim al-Habibi recited to us; Abu Hatim Muhammad ibn Hayyan al-Masni recited to us, and said: "I have not seen anything more complete than it." He said: Muhammad ibn 'Ali al-Halari recited to us a verse by 'Abd Allah al-Mubarak:

Among the signs of affliction for the afflicted is
That you find no withdrawal from your desire.

The slave is the slave of the self in its appetites,
While the free man may be sated at times and hungry at others.

Abu al-Qasim al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Habibi recited to us; Abu al-Hasan 'Isa ibn Zayd al-'Uqayli recited to us; Abu al-Muthanna Mu'adh ibn al-Muthanna al-'Anbari recited to us, from his father, for Abu al-'Atahiyah:

Disobey the desire of the self and do not obey it,
For if you anger it, it will [still] be against you.

Until when will you seek its pleasure,
While it seeks your enmity?

Abu al-Qasim al-Habibi recited to us; Abu 'Ubayd al-Tusi recited to us:

If you give the self its wishes,
It will open its mouth wide toward its desire.

I heard Abu al-Qasim say: I heard Abu Nasr ibn Mansur ibn 'Abd Allah al-Isfahani say in Herat:

I heard Abu al-Hasan 'Amr ibn Wasil al-Bahtari say: Sahl ibn 'Abd Allah al-Tustari was asked about desire, and he said to the questioner: "Your desire commands you; if you oppose it, it will destroy you." And he said: "When two matters present themselves to you and you are uncertain which is better, look at the one farther from your desire, for it..."

Abu al-Qasim al-Habibi recited to us, the Imam Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Isma'il al-Qaffal al-Mashashi in Marw recited to us, and Abu Bakr al-Zaydi recited to me:

When the self demands from you a desire one day,
And there is a path to opposing it,

Leave it and oppose what you desire, for
Your desire is an enemy, and opposition is a friend.

Allah the Glorified and Exalted said:

﴿And Allah has led him astray knowing about him, and has sealed his hearing and his heart, and placed a covering upon his sight.﴾ Hamzah, al-Kisa'i and Khalaf read غَشْوَةً (ghashwatan), with a fatha on the ghayn and without an alif, while the rest read غِشاوَةً (ghishawatan), with an alif and a kasra on the ghayn.

﴿So who will guide him after Allah? Will you not then take heed?﴾ And they said, meaning the polytheists:

﴿There is nothing but our life of this world: we die and we live, and nothing destroys us except time.﴾ "We die and live": the fathers die and the sons live. "And nothing destroys us except time": nothing ends us except the age and the length of life. In the reading of Ibn Mas'ud it is: "And nothing destroys us except time passes."

﴿And they have no knowledge of that; they only conjecture.﴾

Al-Husayn ibn Fanjawayh informed us in my reading: Abu Hudhayfah Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Ali al-Dinawari narrated to us; Abu 'Ubayd 'Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Harb the judge narrated to us; Ahmad ibn al-Miqdam al-'Ijli narrated to us; Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah ibn Abi 'Imran narrated to us, from al-Zuhri, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "The people of the Jahiliyyah used to say: 'It is only the night and the day that destroy us, they cause us to die and they cause us to live.'" Then Allah the Exalted said in His Book: ﴿There is nothing but our life of this world: we die and we live, and nothing destroys us except time﴾, so they curse time.

Allah the Exalted said: "The son of Adam hurts Me: he curses time, while I am Time. In My hand is the command; I alternate the night and the day." [224] [Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 25/198.]

Abu Sa'id Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Hamdun informed us, with my reading to him in Safar of the year 388, and he acknowledged it: Abu Hamid Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan informed us; Muhammad ibn Yahya, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Bishr and Ahmad ibn Yusuf narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq ibn Hammam narrated to us, Ma'mar ibn Rashid informed us, from Hammam ibn Munabbih ibn Kamil ibn Sayj, who said: This is what Abu Hurayrah narrated to us from Muhammad ﷺ, who said: "Allah the Exalted said: Let not the son of Adam say, 'O misfortune of time,' for I am Time. I send the night and the day, and when I wish, I seize them." [225] [Fath al-Bari: 10/466; Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 14/1.]

Abu 'Abd Allah ibn Fanjawayh informed us: 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Samurah narrated to us; 'Abd al-Malik ibn Ahmad al-Baghdadi narrated to us; Mahmud ibn Khadash narrated to us; Sufyan ibn Muhammad al-Thawri narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: "Do not curse time, for Allah the Exalted is Time." [226] [Musnad Ahmad: 2/395.]

Abu 'Ubayd al-Qasim ibn Sallam said in explaining this hadith: This is something that no one among the people of Islam should be ignorant of its meaning. The Arabs' custom was to blame time at the time of calamities and misfortunes, when time destroyed them, the days frightened them, and the age came upon them, and similar things, until they mentioned it in their poetry, [and attributed events to it] (addition from Tafsir al-Qurtubi).

'Amr ibn Qami'ah said:

The daughters of time have shot at me from where I do not see,
So how about one who is shot at and is not a shooter?

If they were arrows, I would have guarded against them,
But I am being shot at with no arrows.

On both palms once, and on a staff,
I rise three times after my standing.

It is related that al-Sha'bi entered upon 'Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan when he had become weak, and [the caliph] asked him about his condition, so he recited these verses:

Time has taken them away this morning,
And time shoots at me and I do not shoot.

O time, you have greatly afflicted us
With our best, and it has settled in our bones.

You have left us as meat upon a chopping block;
If you were to spare any of the meat...

And you have taken from us what you will not return to us.
O time, you have not been just in judgment.

Abu al-Qasim al-Sadusi recited to us; 'Abd al-Sami' ibn Muhammad al-Hashimi recited to us; Abu al-Hasan al-'Absi informed us, about Ibn Lankak on this theme:

Say to time, emptied of nobility, O you ugly in deeds, stern of countenance,
How many a noble man you have brought down to the lowlands, and how many a base man you have raised to the Pleiades.

Abu 'Ubaydah said: I debated with some of the heretics (mulahidah). He said: "Do you not see that He says: 'Indeed Allah is Time'?" I said to him: "Did anyone ever revile Allah in the calamities of time? Rather, they used to say as al-A'sha said:

Allah has taken [the people] for fidelity and justice,
And has turned blame toward the man..."

He said: So the interpretation of the Prophet's saying ﷺ "Indeed Allah is Time" is that Allah, Majestic is His mention, is the One who brings time, hardships and calamities. So if you revile time, the reviling falls upon Allah the Exalted, because He is the doer of these things, its judge and its manager.

Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: Its meaning: "Indeed Allah is the one who makes time (mudahhir al-duhur)."

It is related from 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, in one of his sermons: "The one who makes times, from whom is ease, and from whom is hardship."

The proof of this interpretation is what al-Qasim al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Nisaburi informed us: Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Karizi narrated to us; Abu 'Abd Allah Muhammad ibn al-Qasim al-Jumahi narrated to us; 'Asr ibn Ahmad narrated to us, who said: It reached me that Salim ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar often mentioned time, so Abu 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar rebuked him and said: "O my son, beware of mentioning time," and he recited:

Time is not the one who commits a thing at its time,
Nor the bringer of trials, so do not revile time.

But whenever Allah sends a sender
Upon a people, He makes their ease into hardship.

Abu al-Qasim al-Habibi recited to us; the Shaykh Abu Muhammad Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Muzani recited to us; Mu'adh ibn Najdah ibn al-'Iryan recited to us:

Time turns over matters, for it [if it] has struck you with pains,
And the one who has time upon him for blame, for time only relates the course of pens.

Time is complained of, and is asked for more, but
The command of the King is the support of rulings.

Al-Ustadh Abu al-Qasim recited to us; my father recited to me; Abu 'Ali Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Wahhab al-Thaqafi recited to me:

O one who blames time when it befalls him,
Do not blame time for its excuse.

Time is commanded by one who commands it,
And time ends at his command.

How many a disbeliever has abundant wealth
That increases manifold in his disbelief.

And a believer who has not a dirham
Whose faith increases in his poverty.

﴿And when Our clear verses are recited to them, their argument is nothing but that they say: "Bring our fathers, if you are truthful." Say: "Allah gives you life, then causes you to die, then will gather you to the Day of Resurrection," about which there is no doubt, but most people do not know.﴾ (That is, to the Day of Resurrection.) ﴿And to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. And on the Day the Hour is established, on that Day the falsifiers will lose. And you will see every nation kneeling (jathiyah), gathered, sitting on its knees from the terror of that Day. The root of jathwah is a group of anything.﴾

Tarafah, describing two graves, said:

You see two heaps of earth upon them,
Slabs, hard, of smooth stone.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us: 'Abd Allah ibn Yusuf narrated to us; Musa ibn Muhammad al-Halwani narrated to us; Ya'qub ibn Ishaq al-'Alawi narrated to us; 'Abd Allah ibn Yahya al-Thaqafi narrated to us; Abu 'Ilran narrated to us, from 'Asim al-Ahwal, from Ibn 'Uthman al-Nahdi, from Salman al-Farisi, who said: On the Day of Resurrection there is an hour that lasts ten years, in which people will be kneeling on their knees, until even Ibrahim (peace be upon him) will call out: "I ask nothing of You today except for myself."

﴿Every nation will be called to its record. Today you will be recompensed for what you used to do. This is Our Book, which speaks against you with truth.﴾ In it is the register of the guardians (diwan al-hafazah); and it was said: it is the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz).

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us: 'Umar ibn Nuh al-Bajali narrated to us; Abu Khalifah narrated to us; 'Uthman ibn 'Abd Allah al-Shami narrated to us; 'Uqbah ibn al-Walid narrated to us, from Artat ibn al-Mundhir, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The first thing Allah created was the pen, from light, the distance of whose travel is five hundred years; and the Tablet, from light, the distance of whose travel is five hundred years. He said to the pen: 'Write,' and it wrote what would be until the Day of Resurrection, its coolness and its heat, its moist and its dry." Then he recited this verse: ﴿This is Our Book, which speaks against you with truth.﴾ [228] [al-Mustadrak: 2/498; Fath al-Bari: 6/206; Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 29/22; Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 3/245.]

﴿Indeed We were having your deeds copied.﴾ He said: Can copying (naskh) occur except from a book that has been completed? The meaning of nastansikh is: He commands copying. Al-Dahhak said: "We recorded (nuthbit)." Al-Suddi: "We wrote." Al-Hasan: "We preserved."

﴿As for those who believed and did righteous deeds, their Lord will admit them into His mercy, that is, His Paradise. That is the clear triumph, the pure victory. And as for those who disbelieved: "Were not My verses recited to you? But you were arrogant and were a criminal people."﴾ And when it is said, ﴿"Indeed the promise of Allah is true, and the Hour, there is no doubt about it,"﴾ the common readers read وَالسَّاعَةُ (al-sa'atu) in the nominative, as a beginning (mubtada') with its predicate in what follows; their evidence is His saying: ﴿Indeed the earth belongs to Allah; He gives it as inheritance to whom He wills of His servants, and the final outcome is for the God-fearing.﴾ [Surah al-A'raf: 128.]

Abu Raja' and Hamzah read وَالسَّاعَةَ (al-sa'ata) in the accusative, coordinating it with "the promise." ﴿"There is no doubt in it"﴾ ... ﴿"You said: 'We do not know what the Hour is; we only think it is a conjecture, and we are not certain."﴾ That it will happen. ﴿And there will appear to them the evil of what they did,﴾ that is, its recompense. ﴿And there will surround them what they used to mock.﴾ And it is said: ﴿"Today We will forget you as you forgot the meeting of this your Day,"﴾ that is, We will leave you in the Fire. ﴿As you forgot the meeting of this your Day,﴾ as you abandoned faith in this your Day. ﴿Your refuge is the Fire, and you have no helpers.﴾ ﴿That is because you took the signs of Allah in mockery, and the life of this world deceived you.﴾ ﴿So today they will not be brought out from it,﴾ the common readers read يُخْرَجُونَ (yukhrajuna) with a damma on the ya', while the people of Kufa except 'Asim read it with a fatha on it.

﴿Nor will they be asked to make amends (yustatabun), that is, to be pleased.﴾ ﴿So to Allah belongs all praise, Lord of the heavens and Lord of the earth, Lord of the worlds.﴾ The common readers read رَبِّ (rabbi) with a kasra on the ba' in all three, while Ibn Muhaysin read it in the nominative, meaning "He is the Lord."

﴿And to Him belongs the greatness in the heavens and the earth, and He is the Mighty, the Wise.﴾
